scope.title: Gerak Brown: Donsker, variasi kuadratik, dan waktu kena
scope.audit_kind: independent bounded mathematics and generated-reader static audit
scope.excluded: No source, reader, backend, controls, authority evidence, or other QA artifact was modified. External authority and license truth were not re-audited; this check verifies that the Lab 05 source and generated reader state their frozen authority, rights boundary, provenance, and non-endorsement consistently and visibly.

independent_recomputation.method: Endpoint and hitting probabilities were recomputed from exact integer sums of binomial coefficients divided by 2^n at 80-decimal arithmetic precision. The Gaussian target was evaluated independently from the error-function identity. No embedded R result or rendered numeric cell was used as input.

endpoint_binomial_threshold.evidence: The four thresholds independently recompute to 36, 136, 528, and 2080 and match source and reader.

discrete_reflection_and_hitting.claim: P(M_n>=m)=P(S_n>=m)+P(S_n>=m+1), with parity handled by the two ceiling thresholds.
discrete_reflection_and_hitting.evidence: Exact integer-tail sums at m=sqrt(n) reproduce all four rendered hitting probabilities. Reflection after first contact maps the below-m terminal paths bijectively to terminal paths strictly above m.

brownian_targets.claim: The endpoint target is Phi(1), and the level-one Brownian hitting target is 2(1-Phi(1)).
brownian_targets.evidence: Independent targets 0.8413447460685428 and 0.3173105078629144 round to the source and reader constants.

donsker_interpretation.claim: W_n converges in distribution in C[0,1] under the uniform topology; this is not pathwise convergence. Endpoint evaluation and the maximum functional justify the stated distributional limits at continuity points, while the finite table is diagnostic rather than a proof.

variation_claims.claim: On the natural mesh Q=1 and V=sqrt(n) pathwise; subdividing each linear segment into r equal pieces gives Q=1/r while preserving V=sqrt(n). This fixed-prelimit refinement does not contradict Brownian quadratic variation [B]_1=1.
variation_claims.evidence: Direct algebra gives n*(1/sqrt(n))^2=1, n/sqrt(n)=sqrt(n), and nr*(1/(r*sqrt(n)))^2=1/r. The source explicitly distinguishes the two orders of limits.

deterministic_base_r_contract.note: Rscript was not available on the process PATH; execution determinism was therefore checked statically and by an independent exact arithmetic implementation rather than by launching a second R process.

dependency_rights_and_provenance.visible_non_endorsement: Edisi independen; tidak didukung atau disahkan oleh Kyle Siegrist, Random, atau penulis sumber.

admission_recommendation: The audited source and generated reader are mathematically and statically admissible at these exact hashes.
